title: Multiplication and chart extension are continuous on bundle tests
statement: Let $N$ be a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth real $m$-manifold without boundary [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold], and $E\to N$ a smooth rank-$q$ real vector bundle [def-sfb-smooth-real-vector-bundle]. Use $\mathcal T(E)=\Gamma_c^\infty(E^*\otimes\mathrm{Dens}_N)$, formed with [def-sfb-smooth-dual-bundle], [def-sfb-smooth-density-line], [def-sfb-smooth-tensor-bundle] and endowed with [def-sfb-compact-smooth-section-topology]. (i) For any smooth $h:N\to\mathbf R$, the pointwise operator $M_h:\mathcal T(E)\to\mathcal T(E)$, $M_h\phi=h\phi$, is real-linear and continuous. (ii) For a smooth chart $x:U\to V\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ and a smooth frame $e_1,\ldots,e_q$ of $E|_U$, the formula $J_{x,e}(f)|_U=\sum_{a=1}^q f_a(x)\,e^a\otimes|dx^1\cdots dx^m|$, with zero value off $U$, defines a continuous real-linear map $J_{x,e}:\mathscr D(V,\mathbf R^q)\to\mathcal T(E)$, where $e^a$ is the dual frame and the local test domain has the LF topology of [def-sfb-local-coefficient-tests]. In particular the extended section is smooth.

proof.text: Write $B=E^*\otimes\mathrm{Dens}_N$. Each defining $p$ satisfies $p(s+t)\leq p(s)+p(t)$ and $p(cs)=|c|p(s)$ by the coordinate coefficient, derivative, supremum and norm formulas. In the smallest topology specified in the cited definition, finite intersections of seminorm balls centered at a point form a neighborhood basis: if $t\in s_0+\{p<\epsilon\}$, then $t+\{p<\epsilon-p(t-s_0)\}$ lies in that translate by the triangle inequality; apply this to each of finitely many constraints. These balls are convex. Halving the radii proves continuity of addition, and $p(cs-c_0s_0)\leq |c|p(s-s_0)+|c-c_0|p(s_0)$ proves joint scalar continuity by also keeping $|c|$ bounded near $c_0$. For every smooth section, its support is closed by its definition as a closure, hence compact as a closed subset of compact $N$: extend an open cover by the open complement and take a finite subcover of $N$. Thus the compact-support section space is the whole section space, with the same topology. This verifies the locally convex real topological vector-space hypotheses of the LF criterion.

proof.text: In any smooth chart $y$ and frame $b$ of $B$, the coefficient expression of $M_hs$ is $(h\circ y^{-1})s_{y,b}$. Apply the weighted-composition lemma with $g=\mathrm{id}$ and $A=(h\circ y^{-1})I_q$. It gives smooth coefficients and, for each defining compact $H$ and order $k$, $p_{y,b,H,k}(M_hs)\leq C p_{y,b,H,k}(s)$ with $C$ independent of $s$. The support can only shrink, so the map is well-defined on tests. The pointwise formula is real-linear. For a target neighborhood given by finitely many seminorm inequalities, impose on $s$ the same finitely many inequalities with radii divided by their positive constants $C$; its image lies in that neighborhood. This proves continuity at zero and, by linearity, everywhere, proving (i).

proof.text: Fix a compact $K\subseteq V$ and $f\in\mathscr D_K$. Put $L=x^{-1}(K)\subseteq U$, compact in $N$. Since $N$ is Hausdorff, $L$ is closed: for a point outside $L$, separate it from each point of $L$ and take a finite subcover on $L$; the intersection of the finitely many outside neighborhoods misses $L$. The proposed section is zero on the open set $N\setminus L$. On $U$, its coefficients in the frame $e^a\otimes|dx|$ are $f\circ x$. In another chart $y:W\to Q$ and frame $b$ of $B$, on $U\cap W$ they are $A(z)f(g(z))$, where $g=x\circ y^{-1}$ and $A$ is the coefficient change from $e^a\otimes|dx|$ to $b$. The bundle and dual definitions give smooth coefficient changes. The revised density definition uses coefficient transitions $a\mapsto a/g_{xy}$; specifically the $x$ density generator has coefficient $|\det D(x\circ y^{-1})(z)|$ in the $y$ generator. This is the reciprocal transition to $g_{xy}$ at the corresponding point and is smooth and positive by that definition. The tensor definition makes tensor coefficient changes the Kronecker product, with entries products of the respective transition entries. Consequently $A$ is smooth. The weighted-composition lemma gives smoothness on this overlap. These smooth local coefficients and the zero coefficients on $N\setminus L$ cover $N$ and agree with the displayed formula, hence define a smooth section supported in $L$. Every local test lies in some $\mathscr D_K$, so $J_{x,e}$ is well-defined on all tests. Its formula preserves sums and real scalar multiplication.

proof.text:
For continuity on a fixed $\mathscr D_K$, take any target seminorm $p_{y,b,H,k}$, with $H\subseteq Q$ compact. Set $S=H\cap y(L\cap W)$. This is compact: $L\cap y^{-1}(H)$ is an intersection of two compact closed subsets of the Hausdorff space $N$, contained in $U\cap W$, and its image under $y$ is $S$. On $S$, apply the weighted-composition estimate to the smooth $A$ and $g$ from the preceding step. Off $y(L\cap W)$ the section vanishes on a neighborhood, so all its derivatives vanish. Therefore
$$p_{y,b,H,k}(J_{x,e}f)\leq C\max_{|\beta|\leq k}\sup_{w\in g(S)}\|\partial^\beta f(w)\|\leq C\max_{0\leq j\leq k}\sup_{w\in\mathbf R^m}\|D^jf(w)\|.$$
The last inequality evaluates $D^{|\beta|}f$ on the ordered list of coordinate unit vectors; each has norm one, and the order-zero case is $f$ itself. For $m=0$ only the order-zero multi-index occurs. Each supremum on the right is precisely the norm of one defining derivative map for $\mathscr D_K$, so a finite maximum is a continuous seminorm by its defining topology. As in step 2, finitely many target inequalities give finitely many source inequalities, proving continuity of $J_{x,e}|_{\mathscr D_K}$. If $S$ is empty the target seminorm is zero and the same estimate holds.

proof.text: The section target is a locally convex real topological vector space by step 1; $J_{x,e}$ is real-linear by step 3 and continuous on every fixed-support subspace by step 4. The LF linear continuity criterion therefore proves that $J_{x,e}$ is continuous for the LF topology specified for the local tests. Together with its smooth extension and linearity already proved, this is (ii).
